subject: Re: Coordinate enablement — consolidate windows and standby plan
messages:
From: Shelly Cho <shelly.cho@finthrive.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Cc: onboarding@finthrive.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Enablement sessions — timezone conflict & consolidation request

Hi Jonas / Soojin,

Thanks again for scheduling the two half-day enablement windows next week. We just had a calendar conflict pop up: our CTO and two PMs are only available in the morning Pacific window, but our engineering leads can only make the afternoon slot. Rather than run two parallel half-day sessions (which is heavy on your team), would you be able to consolidate into a single 2.5-hour condensed session that covers the console walkthrough + a focused API enablement lab?

If consolidation isn't feasible, we need a standby plan: run the morning session as the canonical walk-through and record the API lab with a live Q&A office hour for engineering.

Key constraints:
- Primary stakeholders (CTO, Product) available only 08:30–12:30 PST on Tue/Wed next week
- Engineering leads available only after 15:00 PST
- Prefer one invite rather than duplicate sessions

Can you propose two concrete windows (one that targets product stakeholders, one that targets engineering) and a fallback standby plan? Also please confirm whether you can pre-provision API keys and a sandbox so we can hit the endpoints during the lab.

Thanks,
Shelly
Shelly Cho
Head of Professional Services — FinThrive
attachments: none

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Shelly Cho <shelly.cho@finthrive.com>
Cc: soojin.lee@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Enablement sessions — timezone conflict & consolidation request

Hi Shelly — appreciate the heads-up. We can absolutely avoid duplicating work; below are two concrete proposals plus a standby approach. Both options include a 15-minute break and a short live lab for API calls. We can pre-provision sandbox API keys if you provide the list of attendees and IAM roles needed.

Option A (preferred for Product + Eng overlap):
- Tue Nov 30, 2026 | 09:30–12:00 PST (2.5 hrs)
- Agenda: 45m console walkthrough (admin + routing/policy), 15m break, 60m API enablement lab (sample integrations), 30m Q&A/next steps

Option B (better for engineering timezone):
- Wed Dec 1, 2026 | 16:00–18:30 UTC (2.5 hrs) — this aligns with your engineering leads

Standby plan (if stakeholders truly cannot join same session):
- Run Option A as canonical recorded session + 60-minute live office hours the following day for engineers to run labs with our SEs

Action items from our side if you confirm a slot:
- We will provision a sandbox and generate time-bound API keys for each developer (need attendee emails and roles)
- We will attach the Redwood Enablement Checklist and the Enablement Runbook (draft) to the invite
- Requesting an attendee list with one line per person (name / role / email / access needed)

I can take the console walkthrough; Soojin will lead the hands-on lab. Ben will help with runbook and access provisioning.

If either option looks workable, confirm which one and share the attendee list. We will send a calendar invite with links, dial-in, and the Drive materials.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
attachments: Redwood-Enablement-Checklist.pdf (attached), Enablement-Runbook-v1.docx (attached)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Shelly Cho <shelly.cho@finthrive.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 13:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Enablement sessions — timezone conflict & consolidation request

Adding a quick note from the lab side — Option A works best for us if you need product and engineering together. I can run the console walkthrough portion and then pivot into a focused API lab where attendees will pair with SEs on their own sample flows. Please ask your engineering attendees to: 1) confirm they can install the CLI (link in checklist) and 2) provide emails for sandbox keys.

I'll attach the short preflight checklist we run before labs so your team can complete the items a day before:
- Confirm SSO access to the sandbox
- CLI installed (or confirm we provide a browser-based alternative)
- List of test prompts or integration endpoints they'd like to exercise

I left a placeholder in the runbook for 'customer-specific test cases' — if you can drop those in the Drive link below we will bake them into the lab.

Thanks — I will be the primary lab facilitator.

Soojin Lee
Senior SE — Redwood Inference
